20. Mr. Rafique-ul-Huq, learned Advocate has submitted on the other hand that although in an ex-parte proceeding the plaintiff is obliged to prove his own case but still the burden of proof is not as heavy as in a contested case. He has cited some decisions in support of his submission. He has also taken us through the plaint and the evidence owner record and has argued that the plaintiff has proved his case as his assertions both in the plaint and in the evidence of P.W. 1 have gone unrebutted and unchallenged. As a measure of caution he has filed an application for adducing additional evidence of two resolutions which have been quoted in full in the plaint itself. Mr. Moinul Huq has objected to the reception of additional evidence on various grounds. 

 21. As the case was one of no contest, and the plaintiff had a walkover at the trial Court he submitted his case as far as he thought necessary. The two resolutions were quoted in full on the body of the plaint and these were not refuted by the defendants by filing any written statement. He did not adduce any formal proof these two resolutions because none short controverted him. We do not think that we should dismiss his suit altogether because he did not prove and law those two resolutions at the ex-parte hearing had transpired during the course of hearing of the appeal that there were no averments with regard to these two resolutions and the plaintiff-respondent had no evidence at all to offer in respect of these two resolutions then of course we would have considered whether it was at all worth the while to send the case back for retrial. But the plain fact is that the plain have quoted the resolution in fully in the plaint. one controverted them and the suit cannot be dis- missed simply because they did not formally prove the resolutions.
